artifacts.summary: Confirms the phases_total gap in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, documents the shared batch-wide cycle budget pool, measures the real phases-per-cycle distribution from this repo's own metrics.jsonl history (base mode and hard mode), and recommends an admission-time-only advisory notice with a data-grounded threshold (remaining_phases > remaining_cycles*2 base / *1 hard).

memory_candidates.content: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's work-cycle budget is a SHARED BATCH-WIDE POOL (batch_cycle_budget = ntasks * per_task_max_cycles, tested against sum(cycle_counts)), not a per-task-isolated counter. Any feature reasoning about 'remaining cycles' for a task must read batch_cycle_budget - sum(cycle_counts), which reduces to the per-task case only for a batch of one.

Measured from this repo's own specs/**/metrics.jsonl history (138 files, 451 entries): 92% of tasks with a plan complete their entire implement phase in one dispatch regardless of phase count (observed up to 10 phases in one cycle); base-mode multi-cycle advances are right-skewed (mean 1.32, median 1, max 5, n=31); hard-mode advances are observed near-exactly 1 phase/cycle (zero deviation across 15 consecutive cycles in one real task). Raw phase count alone is a weak single-vs-multi-cycle predictor -- totals overlap between the two groups.

phases_total for a plan is derivable BEFORE any handoff exists by grepping the plan file's '### Phase N:' headings via lib/phase-heading-patterns.sh's PHASE_HEADING_ERE -- three call sites already do this (update-task-status.sh count_plan_phases, skill-base.sh skill_corroborate_phase_counts, orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's H1 block for hard-mode plan-path resolution). A fourth phases_total-counting call site is a mechanical port of this existing pattern, not new design.
